title: The general Herbrand proof uses an invalid restriction on contraction.
details: Buss1995 §3 Theorem3 proof uses completeness of the multiplicative one-sided GS calculus when contraction is restricted to quantifier-free formulas and formulas with leading existential. The author erratum explicitly acknowledges this gap. McKinley, A sequent calculus demonstration of Herbrand’s Theorem, arXiv1007.3414v1 pp.1–2, supplies the valid sequent ⊢ (∀x A ∧ ∀x B), ((∃x ¬A ∨ ∃x ¬B) ∧ (∃x ¬A ∨ ∃x ¬B)); every available bottom GS rule other than contraction on the right conjunction has an invalid premise. Thus this conjunction contraction cannot simply be forbidden. Repair: establish deep-contraction admissibility for Herbrand proofs as McKinley does, or restrict adoption to §2 existential/universal-existential extraction. The corpus takes the latter scope and explicitly unions finite witness families under contraction. General Herbrand’s theorem is not refuted. The adjacent defect is not used by the entry; no upstream corrected version of this1995 paper is inferred.
